function: One-bit ML symbol detection for uplink multiuser massive MIMO, learning per-antenna likelihood functions from pilots with dithering and a DNN SNR estimator, no channel estimation (pp. 6-8).
system: Uplink MU-MIMO: BS with 32 or 64 one-bit-ADC antennas, 3 to 6 single-antenna users, 4-QAM or 16-QAM; Rayleigh and geometric mmWave channels (pp. 3, 9-12).
method: Counting-based statistical learning of likelihood functions with antenna-wise Gaussian dithering and adaptive dither power; offline supervised DNN (four hidden layers, ReLU, Adam) estimates SNR (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Simulated i.i.d. Rayleigh fading and a geometric mmWave ULA channel with L = 4 paths; no standardized model, public dataset, or measurements (pp. 9, 12).
test_conditions: Likelihoods learned from 45 or 90 pilot repetitions per symbol vector, data detected in the same block; SNR swept; DNN training details not given (pp. 8-11).
baselines: Non-learned: one-bit ZF with perfect CSI, one-bit ML with perfect or estimated CSI, infinite-bit ML, OSS (coded). Learned: naive learning-based ML, MCD [38] (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Symbol error rate, frame error rate (polar-coded), and number of under-trained likelihood functions versus SNR (pp. 9-12).
q1_support: p. 9: "We consider Rayleigh fading model". I.i.d. CN(0,1) Rayleigh channels, plus a custom geometric mmWave ULA model in Sec. VI-D (page 12); the only 3GPP mention (page 4) bounds the number of users, not the channel.
q2_support: p. 3: "Nt time slots and a data transmission phase with Nd slots". Likelihoods are learned from the pilots of each block and applied to the data of the same block; each setting (users, antennas, QAM order, Ntr, channel type) is a separate run, with nothing trained in one condition and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 10: "Minimum-Center-Distance (MCD) [38]". Learned baselines MCD (Fig. 9, 16-QAM) and the naive learning detector; non-learned one-bit ZF with perfect CSI [19] and one-bit ML with estimated CSI; all compared in symbol error rate (Figs. 6, 7, 9).
q4_support: p. 13: "solution for 6G applications". The conclusion calls the method low-complexity, which is qualitative; no FLOPs, parameter count, runtime or complexity order is reported, and training cost appears only as the pilot count K Ntr, which is signaling overhead.
q5_support: p. 12: "we adopt a geometric channel model whose number of channel". All data are self-generated Rayleigh and geometric channels; no link to code or data, public dataset or measurement appears in the 14 pages.
notes: PDF is the arXiv v2 (arXiv:2304.07696v2, 22 Mar 2024) and carries no DOI, so the DOI-title match cannot be checked from the PDF; title and content fit an IEEE TVT 2024 paper. Eligibility is a judgment call: the learned parts are the counting-based learning of per-antenna likelihood functions from pilots (non-neural) and an offline-trained DNN SNR estimator used inside the detector (page 8); the reviewer may confirm that this counts as a learned component of detection. q2: all learning is per coherence block from pilots, and the training conditions of the SNR-estimator DNN are not described. q3: MCD [38] is compared only in the 16-QAM case (page 10); the naive detector of Sec. III is presented as a preliminary approach, and page 1 says part of this work appeared at GLOBECOM 2019 [1], but the paper does not state that the naive detector comes from [1], so MCD [38] is the clear published learned baseline.
